title: Promoting Saturday dances and the picnic admission
summary: Dances were promoted by word of mouth on Saturday nights and Sunday afternoons, and the ballgame picnic charged 15 cents.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: But when you had that homemade band, you know, you said you'd play in a little house, you'd find an empty house or something.
Yeah, I'd promote the...
Would they be just deserted houses? I mean, people left?

Well, just people move out, you know, change from one plantation to another, you know. Uh-huh. There's always an empty house, you know. And sometimes we get in the finish. People didn't have much furniture, you know. They let us come in the house and have the party.
How would you promote it?
We'd give them all the food and the beer they wanted, you know.
How would you promote or advertise it? Huh? How would you promote a thing like that in advance?
Oh, from mouth to mouth.
Mouth to mouth. Yeah.

Well, there were people around there, they'd all look for a place to go on Saturday night, you see. No place to go. They'd all flop there and get beer. What kind of plantation was this? Oh, the big sugarcane plantation. Sugarcane plantation. Yeah, big sugar mill and everything.
Oh, yeah?
And all the people from the little villages, other plantation would come.
When would you do it usually on? Saturday night or what?
Saturday night. Saturday night. Saturday night. Saturday and Sunday afternoon.
I see. Saturday night and Sunday afternoon.
They would let me run on Sunday night. They said people had to go to work early, Monday.
Monday, yeah.

I start early on Sunday afternoon, you see. Uh-huh. And when I gave them a big picnic at the park, I really charged 15 cents to come in. Uh-huh. After the game, everyone went out and came out and bought their tickets.
Oh, you first had to get out? Get out.
That paid admission to see the game. Yeah. After coming by me then, you see.
I see. Right in the baseball park, huh?
Yeah. Yeah.
